vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: benchmark-store
Version: 1.1.0

The benchmark-store skill bundle is a legitimate framework designed for managing, storing, and executing benchmarks to evaluate AI agent skills. It provides a structured approach to quality assessment through SQLite-based database management (scripts/benchmark_db.py), Pareto front tracking (scripts/pareto.py), and interfaces for handling immutable 'frozen' benchmarks and encrypted 'hidden' tests (interfaces/hidden_tests.py). While the bundle includes datasets containing security attack patterns like SQL injection and XSS (data/test-cases.yaml and data/red-team-guide.md), these are explicitly used as reference data for 'red-team' testing to ensure other skills are robust. The implementation lacks any signs of data exfiltration, unauthorized remote execution, or malicious prompt injection, and its behavior aligns perfectly with its stated purpose of providing evaluation standards and baselines.

llm.summary: The skill is generally coherent with a local benchmark store (stores frozen tests, SQLite DB, Pareto checks) but there are mismatches between the SKILL.md CLI examples and the actual code (compare requires an evaluator callable), plus minor metadata inconsistencies — review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md and included code files (benchmark_db.py, frozen_benchmark, hidden_tests, pareto) all align: the package provides storage and local benchmarking/pareto checks. No network calls, no credentials, and the requested resources are proportional to a benchmark store. Minor mismatch: SKILL.md frontmatter version (0.1.0) differs from registry version (1.1.0), which is a metadata inconsistency but not a functional security problem.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md shows CLI examples (e.g. 'compare --skill-path /path/to/skill') that imply the script will run a comparison end-to-end. However, scripts/benchmark_db.py's compare_with_benchmark explicitly requires an evaluator callable and raises a ValueError if none is provided — the truncated main() may or may not wire an evaluator. This is an important coherence issue: the docs/CLI could mislead users into running a compare that either fails or (if an evaluator is auto-wired in other truncated code) might execute code from a provided skill path. Also, HiddenTest loading APIs accept a password and can decrypt hidden tests — expected for hidden-tests functionality, but be mindful that any password-based decryption will require secrets supplied at runtime (not declared in requires.env).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only install (no install spec). The skill includes local Python scripts and libraries only (stdlib + sqlite3). Nothing is downloaded or executed from external URLs, so install risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, no credentials declared, and required config paths are not requested. The code performs local file and DB I/O which is consistent with the stated purpose. Note: HiddenTest data sources accept a password parameter at runtime (used to unlock encrypted hidden tests) — the SKILL.md does not declare a required secret but the library supports providing one when loading hidden tests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-on (always: false). It does write/read local files (SQLite DB, exported JSON) which is appropriate for a benchmark store. It does not request to modify other skills' configuration or system-wide settings based on the reviewed files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a local benchmark store: it reads/writes a SQLite DB, manages frozen and hidden test data, and performs Pareto/regression checks — all locally. Two things to check before installing or running: (1) The SKILL.md CLI examples imply an automatic 'compare' operation, but the compare function in scripts/benchmark_db.py requires an evaluator callable (or will raise a ValueError). Confirm how the CLI's main() wires an evaluator before running compare; otherwise compare may fail or behave unexpectedly. (2) When you run comparisons, you may pass a path to a 'skill' that could be executed/evaluated by an evaluator — only run comparisons on skills you trust or run inside a sandbox. If you plan to use hidden tests, be prepared to supply a password at runtime to decrypt test data; SKILL.md does not declare this secret explicitly. If these points are acceptable, the skill’s code and instructions are consistent with its purpose and there are no obvious network exfiltration or credential requests. If you need higher assurance, ask for the full, untruncated main() and any remaining scripts so you can confirm there are no implicit evaluators that execute untrusted code or call external endpoints.
